current.text: Coach Dusty May says Flagg will play positions one through four this season, including some guard.
Kyrie Irving is back and Dusty May is the new head coach, so Flagg's role may change.
Playing him at the four next to other power forwards would be a worse fantasy situation for him than a guard role.
Experts see Flagg as Dallas's first offensive priority, ahead of Kyrie Irving. Kyrie should take shots mostly from other players. He may cut Flagg's assists a little.
Dallas has very few ball handlers besides Kyrie Irving. Most of the roster is forwards.
Dallas has too many power forwards, so Flagg will not get many chances to put up big block numbers.
He is expected to improve in year two. His scoring and efficiency should rise, his assists should go over 5, and his steals or blocks could go up.
The main worry is whether his shooting improves.
Josh expects him to start this season close to the level he finished last season at.
Dusty May says he will push Flagg to take more threes.
Pick 9 or the end of round one is a fair price in 9-cat drafts. Pick 7 is a little high. His worst case is about 16th overall, so the downside at pick 9 is small.
His draft position is rising. He went 8th, ahead of Anthony Edwards, in a recent mock.
Josh values him at about 40 USD in an auction and called a 42 USD price high. An average price of 60 USD is way too high.
Dallas has a 4-4-4 fantasy playoff schedule, probably the best in the league, but also a league-high 16 back-to-backs.
Dallas has a two-game week in the matchup starting March 1.
Dallas does not control its own draft pick, so it has no reason to tank.

durable.text: He won Rookie of the Year. He finished 36th in category leagues and 14th over the final two months, beating his ADP of 42. Dallas gave him about 31% usage in 32 minutes after the deadline.
He is a 6'11 forward who handles the ball. On offense he is a high-usage scorer and distributor. On defense he protects the rim from the weak side.
As a rookie he protected the rim less than Josh hoped.
He is called a budding superstar, with superstar-level usage, ball handling and defense.
More perimeter play would probably hurt his rebounds and blocks. Playing the four would not hurt his assists.
Three-point shooting is a weakness. He shot about 29% from three as a rookie, and 27% from three and 44% from the field after the deadline.
Josh sees upside in his shooting.
He helps in PTS, REB, AST, STL, BLK and FT%. His rebounds and blocks are strong for a G,F player.
Turnovers are his weakest category, at about 2.5 per game. His threes are slightly below the pool.

note: Both sites rank him about 10th. Yahoo values him at 47 USD (average cost 51 USD) and ESPN at 55 USD, while Josh's auction value is about 40 USD and he went for only 25 USD in our league last season. Paying above 50 USD prices in the year-two jump that experts expect. He fits punt TO builds and gives rebounds and blocks from a G slot. Early in the season, check whether Dusty May uses him at guard or at the four, whether his three-point volume and accuracy rise, and whether the crowded frontcourt cuts his blocks.
